name: The Brass Meridian
image_style: Cinematic gouache and finely etched travel-chronicle illustration, with dry-brush grain, restrained medieval architectural detail, softly weathered paper texture, and moonlit atmospheric depth. The mood is reverent, curious, and gently absurd: a solemn historical world interrupted by an impeccably serious outsider. Use an unusual palette of deep petrol-black, tarnished chartreuse, smoked lilac, oxidized copper, and pale bone, with controlled chiaroscuro and broad uncluttered shadow shapes. Compose as one striking 16:10 landscape wallpaper at preferably 2560x1600, keeping the entire top edge quiet and leaving a calm dark region for desktop widgets. No lettering, logos, UI, watermark, frame, or decorative border.
scene: At blue hour on a windswept medieval caravan road outside a walled Levantine hill town, a small, accurately rendered band of Crusader-era pilgrims and mounted guards pauses respectfully beside an ancient stone milestone and a distant monastery silhouetted against rose-gold mountains. Space Ghost stands awkwardly at the roadside in his recognizable muscular white costume, black hood and mask, yellow cape, and red power bands, rigidly saluting the milestone as though it were a strategic command post; his cape catches the same wind as the pennants, but he remains clearly separate from all sacred buildings and Christian subjects. The historical figures continue their quiet journey without worshipping or venerating him. Place him in the lower-right third, with the road leading toward the town and a spacious, nearly empty indigo sky across the upper half; affectionate understated humour, reverent medieval atmosphere, no text or lettering.
